title: Reactions that never really stop
question: What does it mean for a reaction to be at equilibrium?
hook: A sealed flask can look perfectly still while reactions inside it keep running in both directions.
idea: At equilibrium the forward and reverse reactions run at equal, non-zero rates, so nothing seems to change overall.

beats.prompt: A flask holds reactants and products, and their concentrations have stopped changing. What is going on inside?

choices.label: Forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates
Both reactions have stopped completely
choices.feedback: It tempts because nothing visibly changes, but the rates are generally not zero, only equal.

choices.label: Only the forward reaction continues until the reactants run out
choices.feedback: It tempts because reactions seem to head one way, but a reverse reaction is running too and cancels the net change.

beats.explain: At equilibrium the forward reaction proceeds at the same rate as the reverse reaction, so there are no net changes in concentrations.

beats.prompt: match each phrase to its meaning
pairs: Rates are not zero, but equal
beats.explain: The position describes how far the reaction has gone, while dynamic equilibrium describes the equal, ongoing rates.

beats.prompt: one step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: A sealed mixture reaches a point where concentrations no longer change.
The forward and reverse reactions then run at equal rates.
Equal rates must mean both reactions are at zero.
So there is no net change in concentrations.
beats.explain: The forward and backward rates are generally not zero. They are equal, which is why concentrations do not change overall.

beats.prompt: Two identical mixtures start reacting, and one has a catalyst added. What is different once both reach equilibrium?

choices.label: Nothing about the equilibrium constant, but the catalysed mixture got there faster
The catalysed mixture has a larger equilibrium constant
choices.feedback: It tempts because catalysts seem to help products form, but they speed up both directions equally.

choices.label: The catalysed mixture never reaches equilibrium
choices.feedback: It tempts because catalysts are not consumed, but they speed both reactions and so equilibrium is reached sooner.

beats.explain: A catalyst affects the forward and reverse reactions in the same way, so it does not change the equilibrium constant, and it speeds up reaching equilibrium.
